title: Colorado recycling and composting rate rises to 16.7% for 2025
h1: Colorado kept 16.7% of its waste out of landfills in 2025, up a point, as composting grows
description: Colorado diverted 16.7% of municipal waste from landfills in 2025, up from 15.7% in 2024, as cities expanded composting, The Colorado Sun reported.
standfirst: The state has trailed much of the country on recycling for years. A tenth annual report from two nonprofits credits city composting programs and newer state laws for the gain.
keywords: Colorado recycling rate 2025, Colorado waste diversion, State of Recycling and Composting Colorado, Eco-Cycle CoPIRG report, Denver compost collection, Longmont recycling ordinance
takeaways: Colorado's landfill diversion rate was 16.7% in 2025, up from 15.7% in 2024, according to state health department figures cited by The Colorado Sun.
The state diverted 29% more food scraps and yard trimmings in 2025 than in 2023.
At least 23 Colorado communities now guarantee recycling for single-family homes, up from 12 in 2017.
body: Colorado recycled or composted a slightly larger share of its trash last year. The portion of waste kept out of municipal landfills reached 16.7% in 2025, up from 15.7% in 2024, The Colorado Sun reported on November 25, 2026, citing figures from the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment.

Composting is the biggest factor, according to the 10th annual State of Recycling and Composting report from the nonprofits Eco-Cycle and CoPIRG Foundation. The groups' summary of the report, released November 16, says the state diverted 29% more food scraps and yard trimmings in 2025 than in 2023. Organic material that rots in a landfill produces methane.

• Denver added compost collection for about 50,000 more households, for 80,400 in total, and has diverted 67,656 tons of organic material since 2023.
  • Aspen businesses diverted 2,303 tons of organic waste in 2025, up from 804 tons in 2023, after the city adopted an organic waste ordinance.
  • Longmont's commercial diversion rate rose from 35% in 2023 to 62% in 2026 under its universal recycling ordinance.
"The big progress has been in organics over the last ten years," Danny Katz, CoPIRG's executive director, told the Sun.

At least 23 Colorado communities now guarantee recycling for single-family residents, up from 12 in 2017, the groups said. Curbside organics collection is provided or required in at least 13 communities, up from five. The report also estimates the state has avoided between 4.1 billion and 5.8 billion single-use checkout bags under its plastic bag law, and says the PaintCare program has collected 8.3 million gallons of leftover paint since 2015.

The groups say all Coloradans are due to have recycling access by 2030 under the state's producer responsibility program for packaging and paper, which is funded by fees on packaging. Grants from that program are now reaching towns including Dolores and Cortez, and applications are open to other communities, the Sun reported. The nonprofits are also urging a state rule requiring large generators to keep food scraps and yard waste out of landfills.

faq.a: Colorado diverted 16.7% of municipal waste from landfills through recycling and composting in 2025, up from 15.7% in 2024, according to state figures reported by The Colorado Sun.

faq.q: When will all Coloradans have access to recycling?
faq.a: By 2030, according to Eco-Cycle and CoPIRG Foundation, under the state's producer responsibility program for packaging and paper.
